description:
## Goal

A reached protocol callback whose receiver type is only partly covered by known or demandable implementations must fail compilation with a stable source diagnostic for the uncovered receiver region. It must not silently route the entire union to one overlapping implementation or reach artifact/interpreter execution with absent values.

This complements fz-kdt.149: that ticket covers a receiver with no applicable implementation; this ticket covers a union with at least one applicable arm and at least one uncovered arm.

## Current state

Pinned clean `origin/main`: `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`.

`fixtures2/00429_external_impl_residual.fz` calls `Sizer.size/1` from `describe/1` with receiver type `int | float`, while only `Sizer.Integer` exists.

Production results:

- `fz2 interp`: exit 1 with `backend value 2 is unbound`.
- `fz2 run`: exit 101 after `artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan`, then panics because continuation `ValueId(2)` is `Absent`.
- `fz2 build`: same diagnostic/panic and creates no executable.

The activation dump resolves `describe/1[int | float]` directly to `Sizer.Integer.size/1(int)`; there is no residual protocol-stub destination. The backend then marks the receiver absent even though `main` still needs its Float constituent across a continuation.

In `resolve_protocol_call`, overlapping implementations are collected into `matches`. Provider discovery and unresolved handling run only when `matches.is_empty()`. Once the Integer implementation overlaps any portion of `int | float`, the function returns a resolved summary without calculating or rejecting the uncovered `float` region. With one target, `call_destinations` lowers this as an unconditional direct call.

The nominal `external_provider_protocol_impl_stays_as_stub_fallback` test is false-green: it discards `compiler.drive()` and leaves the intended assertion as a TODO. Current dispatch documentation explicitly says protocol dispatch has no residual stub outcome.

## Strategy

1. Replace the false-green 00429 test with a red assertion over the semantic partial-coverage outcome and final diagnostic.
2. During protocol resolution, compute implementation coverage over the full receiver type, including providers that may still land.
3. Distinguish complete coverage, transient uncovered coverage awaiting a relevant provider, wholly uncovered coverage, and terminal partial coverage.
4. Emit the terminal diagnostic while protocol names, receiver types, uncovered residual, provider facts, and source span remain available.
5. Keep artifact lowering as a backstop; do not repair this by retaining absent values, inventing a residual stub, or treating one overlapping target as covering the whole receiver.
6. Document the complete-coverage requirement for protocol receiver unions.

## Signal

Add semantic coverage tests for `int | float` with only Integer implementation (terminal residual `float`), the same call while a Float provider can still land (transient wait), both implementations available (resolved two-arm dispatch), and the wholly uncovered case from fz-kdt.149. Add an undeferred three-door diagnostic fixture for 00429.

## Acceptance

- Fixture 00429 emits one fatal `type/protocol-no-impl` diagnostic naming `Sizer.size/1`, receiver `int | float`, and uncovered region `float`, at the protocol-call source span.
- `interp`, `run`, and `build` exit nonzero with the same diagnostic contract. None reports an unbound backend value, `Absent` materialization, Rust panic, or backtrace.
- `build` creates no executable.
- Adding a Float implementation makes the union completely covered and produces runtime type-test dispatch to both implementations.
- The false-green planner test and TODO-only residual-stub expectation are removed.
- Protocol and dispatch documentation describe full receiver coverage and terminal partial coverage.
- Focused semantic/artifact tests, three-door fixture matrix, full library tests, formatting, and clippy with warnings denied pass.
title: Diagnose partially uncovered protocol receiver unions before artifact lowering
